items.title: fix(query): reject malformed Content-Type tokens
items.body:
`requireContentType()` accepted malformed values such as `application/json/extra`, `application/json junk`, and `application/(json)` when a wildcard matched. Exact accepted types sent these malformed values to the 415 branch instead of the documented 422 branch.

Validate the complete type/subtype as HTTP tokens before matching accepted types, following [RFC 9110 sections 8.3.1 and 5.6.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-media-type). Existing wildcard matching, parameter handling, case normalization, and valid token punctuation are preserved. No API or dependency changes.

Fixes #1633.

Validation with Node 24:

- New matrix cases: 36 failures on main across web/Node and exact/subtype/full wildcards; eight valid-token controls pass before and after. All 82 query tests pass with the fix.
- `pnpm test`: lint, TypeScript, and all 73 test files pass; **3,174 tests passed, 51 skipped**, with no type errors. Statement coverage: 96.25%.
- `pnpm build` passes. Built Node and generic entry points return 422 for the malformed examples and 200 for a valid type.

This contribution is AI-assisted.

items.title: fix(body): clean up cancelled request streams
items.body:
`getRequestWebStream()`'s Node fallback adds `data`/`end`/`error` listeners to `event.node.req` when the stream is created and never removes them. If the stream is cancelled while the client is still sending, the next chunk calls `controller.enqueue()` on a closed stream and throws `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_STATE]: Invalid state: Controller is already closed` outside any handler. It also enqueues every chunk regardless of demand, so a fast upload is buffered in memory while the handler is busy.

This makes the bridge lazy and pull-based. The stream uses `highWaterMark: 0`; a Web stream that is never read doesn't touch the request, so Node's own drain and `readRawBody()` behave as before. No new imports.

- The first `pull()` checks the request first: an errored request rejects with its error; if the response already finished while the upload was incomplete, it rejects with `Response already finished`; an ended request closes; a destroyed one rejects with an `aborted` error (`ECONNRESET`). Otherwise it attaches the listeners and resumes the request. A request that closes later without `end` or `error` rejects a pending read with the same `aborted` error.
- Each chunk is enqueued and the request is paused again unless another read is already waiting (`enqueue()` can call `pull()` synchronously for it).
- `cancel()` removes the listeners and resumes the request, so the rest of the upload drains and the handler can still respond (e.g. 413).
- When the response finishes, the listeners are removed and the request is resumed, so a handler that read part of the body and returned without cancelling doesn't leave the upload paused on a keep-alive socket. A read still pending at that point, or any later one, rejects with `Response already finished` rather than hanging or ending as if the upload were complete.

Tests (`test/body.test.ts`): cancel then keep sending, then respond (no uncaught error, listeners released, response delivered), also with the upload still open; an unread 8 MiB body stays bounded after one read; two concurrent reads; a request that ended or was aborted before the first read; a first read after the response finished; a request closed without an error while a read is pending; a pending read when the response finishes; keep-alive reuse after an unused Web body, after `toWebRequest()` + `readRawBody()`, and after a partial Web body read. `pnpm test` (369) and `pnpm build` pass.

items.title: fix(query): validate media type tokens in requireContentType
items.body:
Resolves #1633

### Summary of Changes

- **Media Type Token Validation:** Per [RFC 9110 §8.3.1 and §5.6.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-media-type), a media type consists of `<type>/<subtype>` where `type` and `subtype` must each be a valid HTTP `token` (`1*tchar`).
  - Previously, `requireContentType` only verified `slash <= 0 || slash === mediaType.length - 1`, allowing malformed Content-Type values with multiple slashes (e.g. `application/json/extra`), whitespace (e.g. `application/json junk`), or delimiters (e.g. `application/(json)`) to erroneously match when wildcard acceptance (e.g. `application/*`) was used.
  - Replaced the simple slash index check with `MEDIA_TYPE_RE = /^[!#$%&'*+\-.^_`|~0-9a-zA-Z]+\/[!#$%&'*+\-.^_`|~0-9a-zA-Z]+$/`, ensuring malformed media types consistently throw `422 Unprocessable Content` regardless of whether exact or wildcard matching is configured.
- **Tests:**
  - Added unit test in `test/query.test.ts` verifying that extra slashes, embedded whitespace, and invalid delimiter characters reject with 422 under wildcard acceptance.
  - All 3,120 tests pass across the entire suite.
